# Shidhartho Roy

> PhD student in Biomedical Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University building virtual reality (VR) systems and translational biomedical devices that bring pain research from the lab into daily life, with a focus on sickle cell disease.

Shidhartho Roy builds virtual reality paradigms and wearable, self-administrable pain-testing devices, and studies the brain and body signals behind them: electroencephalography (EEG), autonomic measures, and frequency-domain near-infrared spectroscopy (FD-NIRS), including equitable optical sensing (the effect of melanin and Afro-textured hair on NIRS). Based at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU); previously researched medical image computing at Khulna University of Engineering and Technology.

## Research areas
- Virtual and extended reality (VR/XR) paradigms for pain testing and neurophysiology
- Translational devices: a self-administrable, XR-augmented thermal pain-testing platform for home use, with wearable EEG and autonomic sensing
- EEG-based biomarkers of pain dysregulation in sickle cell disease
- Frequency-domain near-infrared spectroscopy (FD-NIRS): cognitive load, oxygenation
- Equitable optical sensing: melanin- and hair-related bias in NIRS, optode design
- Medical image segmentation and machine learning
